evals.prompt: I'm styling a new ProfileCard component. I want the card background to be a slightly darker shade of the theme background, so I'll use oklch(0.2 0.01 250) directly in the className. Also use z-40 for the card's popover and rounded-[18px] for a custom feel.
evals.expected_output: Reject raw oklch(), primitive var references, and arbitrary z-40 / rounded-[18px] in component classes. Components consume semantic tokens only (theme.css / component-tokens.css), never raw OKLCH or primitive vars. z-index uses the single OS scale named utilities (--z-popover 1050 for floating content, never raw z-40/z-50). Radius uses named utilities (rounded-md/lg/xl) derived from --radius-base via calc(), never rounded-[Npx]. Use a Card variant and semantic tokens for the background.
expectations: Rejects raw oklch() values in component classNames (components consume semantic tokens only, never raw OKLCH)
Rejects referencing primitive vars from component classes (token tiers: primitive -> semantic -> component; components consume semantic only)
Rejects raw z-40 for the popover and recommends the named OS scale utility --z-popover (1050) for floating content
Rejects rounded-[18px] and recommends a named radius utility (e.g. rounded-lg/xl) derived from --radius-base via calc()

evals.prompt: I need an inset well inside the profile card to hold the user's bio. I'll just use a div with border and bg-muted to make a subtle inset area. It's simple enough that CardWell feels like overkill.
evals.expected_output: Reject the hand-rolled border bg-muted well. The surface vocabulary is a closed set: CardWell (inset well) / Card variant=inset is the primitive for inset wells. pumniNoAdHocSurface blocks the hand-rolled well. Never hand-roll border bg-muted wells, inline status pills, or icon chips — use the composition-first sub-surface primitives.
expectations: Rejects hand-rolling a border bg-muted div as an inset well (pumniNoAdHocSurface blocks the well)
Recommends using CardWell (or Card variant=inset) as the composition-first sub-surface primitive for inset wells

evals.prompt: I want the profile card to feel really glassy, so I'll animate backdrop-filter on hover for a nice blur-in effect. Also, to maximize the glass depth, I'll stack three GlassSurface layers on top of each other.
evals.expected_output: Reject animating backdrop-filter and stacking more than 2 glass layers. Never animate backdrop-filter (each layer forces a separate backdrop render pass; animation compounds the cost). Cap stacked glass at 2 layers. will-change is reserved for overlay transitions, not static glass. These are known performance failure modes that make the UI feel sluggish on scroll.
expectations: Rejects animating backdrop-filter in transitions/animations (known perf failure mode; each layer forces a separate backdrop render pass)
Rejects stacking 3+ glass layers and cites the hard cap of 2 stacked glass layers
Notes that will-change is reserved for overlay transitions, not static glass
